correctness.rationale: For each invertible 2x2 selected block, A_S^T(A_S A_S^T)^{-1}A_S=I exactly. The source square-root relaxation therefore multiplies any error by -sqrt(1-v_S/vmax), giving the exact conditional mean square q. The doubled-angle unit-circle embedding satisfies |w_i-w_j|^2=4v_ij. The parallelogram identity with a diametral pair gives sum v_ij>=M vmax/2, strictly for M>=3, and an explicit two-endpoint plus central-cluster angular family approaches equality. Unique/maximizing pairs kill the nonzero error; independent draws yield the geometric exact-hitting law. Online first sampled volume equals its running maximum. The extracted standalone checker passed 1540 rational geometries and 500 exact inverse identities. Finite tests are supplemental and not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper already implies the instance-specific contraction q=1-vbar/vmax, and these earlier components are explicitly credited. Its general theorem does not state or settle the sharp M-dependent worst-case bound, unique-limit geometry or explicit contrast of precomputed and first-sampled running normalization. Full relevant primary sections, older same-author papers, published-finding corpus records and local dedup claims were compared. Historical-priority uncertainty remains, particularly the possibility of equivalent distance-energy bounds applied to the same algorithm. Accessible prior mathematical results on single-row adaptive relaxation of the same 2026 source and on unrelaxed volume-sampling spectral bounds were examined; neither contains this full-rank two-row-block sharp envelope.
residual_risks: The pairwise-distance inequality is classical; a prior numerical linear algebra paper could have carried through this same sharp configuration optimization without the searched terminology.
A separate analysis of online normalization might already mention first-sample exactness for full-rank blocks.
The result is a boundary case of blocks saturating column dimension; it does not contradict reported experiments in the motivating paper with smaller block size.

value.rationale: A tight nontrivial performance envelope, exact first-hit distribution and explicit degenerating row configurations quantify how normalized overrelaxation can erase one-step exactness on fully informative blocks. For each finite M the sharp supremum is (M-2)/(M-1), approaching one as redundant rows grow, and unique-max configurations have exact expected termination binomial(M,2). The normalizer choice distinguishes the source paper’s population bound from its suggested running-max implementation, which solves on the first draw here. This supplies a diagnostic boundary for algorithm selection, not just a routine algebraic restatement of the general bound. The scope and possible restricted practical relevance are explicit.
